questions.q: What problem does a Payment Process Request (PPR) solve?
options: It eliminates the need for any approvals on invoices
It lets many due invoices be selected, grouped, and paid together instead of one at a time
It replaces the need for a supplier record
It converts all invoices to a single currency
questions.explain: A PPR batches the payment of many eligible invoices at once, which scales far better than paying each individually.

questions.q: Put these PPR stages in order: Build Payments, Selection, Review, Build Proposed Payments.
options: Selection, Build Proposed Payments, Review, Build Payments
Review, Selection, Build Payments, Build Proposed Payments
Build Payments, Review, Selection, Build Proposed Payments
Build Proposed Payments, Build Payments, Selection, Review
questions.explain: A PPR moves from Selection, to grouping into Build Proposed Payments, through Review, and finally to Build Payments.

questions.q: What is a "pay group" used for in a PPR?
options: Setting the exchange rate for foreign currency invoices
Determining the GL account an invoice posts to
Categorizing invoices (e.g., Employees vs. Trade Suppliers) so separate PPRs can target different populations
Setting the matching type applied to an invoice
questions.explain: Pay group lets an organization run distinct payment processes for different categories of payees.

questions.q: In the Solace Robotics example, why was one supplier's invoice pulled from the batch during review?
options: The invoice had already been paid
The invoice exceeded the PPR's maximum payment amount
The supplier's bank account was invalid
A credit memo affecting that invoice was expected imminently
questions.explain: The AP supervisor removed that supplier's invoice during the review stage because of an imminent credit memo.

questions.q: Why does a PPR include a review step before building final payments?
options: It is a legally mandated waiting period with no other purpose
It gives a person a deliberate checkpoint to confirm the batch makes sense before money moves
It automatically recalculates every invoice's tax
It is only required for international payments
questions.explain: The review stage preserves human judgment in an otherwise automated batch process, catching issues before payments are finalized.
